item.text: {"errors":[{"what":"“Solid (−)” is used in the legend, but the stimulatory arrows from the hypothalamus to the pituitary and from the pituitary to the ovary are also solid.","why_wrong":"The same line style represents both forward stimulation and negative feedback, so the legend can mislead students about what the forward arrows mean.","severity":"misleading"},{"what":"“Dotted (−): inhibin B from granulosa cells suppresses FSH only.”","why_wrong":"Inhibin B is especially relevant in the follicular phase, but inhibin A also suppresses FSH and is prominent in the luteal phase. Naming only B in a whole-cycle diagram may imply it is the only ovarian inhibin involved.","severity":"misleading"},{"what":"The node labels, feedback labels, and legend are very small within a large image with substantial blank space below the figure.","why_wrong":"Several labels are difficult to read at the supplied size, although none appears clipped or overlapping.","severity":"cosmetic"}],"legibility":3,"teaches_caption":true,"overall":7,"verdict":"The axis and three feedback relationships are largely correct and support the caption. Clarify the solid-line convention, add the role of inhibin A, and enlarge the diagram text."}
